explanation: James Watt, born in 1736, later made steam engines far more efficient with his separate condenser, patented in 1769. By then Newcomen-style engines had been draining mines for over 50 years.

claims.text: Thomas Newcomen's steam engine began pumping water from a coal mine near Dudley, England, in 1712.
James Watt was born in 1736, Richard Trevithick in 1771 and George Stephenson in 1781, so none of them built the 1712 engine.
James Watt patented his separate condenser in 1769, making steam engines much more efficient.
Newcomen-type engines had been pumping water from mines for more than 50 years by 1769.
